transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. How can I help you today?
Hello, Doctor. Lately I just can’t think straight or make decisions at work the way I used to. It’s making it really hard to do my job at the warehouse, and I just don't know what's going on with me.
Have you been having trouble focusing or remembering things, or does your mind feel unusually slow or foggy most days?

Yes, Doctor, it really does feel like my head is full of mud most days. I'll read the numbers on a report and they just don't stick in my mind at all. Even simple choices, like which supervisor to put on which shift, can take me all morning because I keep second-guessing myself.
How long have you been feeling this way? Has this mental fog and difficulty making decisions been going on for at least two weeks, or longer?

It’s been much longer than two weeks, Doctor. This current slump has been dragging on since around last fall, so it's been weighing me down for almost a year now. Honestly, I've had these ups and downs off and on for at least a couple of years, but this low spell is really wearing me out.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were ["F32", "F33", "F43.2"], but based on this conversation, F32 (episodic depressive episode) is less likely because the patient reports a current low mood lasting almost a year with a history of recurrent episodes over at least two years, which meets the criteria for recurrent depressive disorder (F33). F43.2 (adjustment disorder with mixed anxiety and depressed mood) is also less likely because the duration and persistence of symptoms exceed typical adjustment disorder, which usually arises within one month of a stressor and resolves within six months. The chronic, recurring nature of the cognitive and decision-making difficulties strongly supports F33.

F06.0 (organic mood disorder) is less likely because there is no clear evidence of a primary neurological or medical condition affecting cognition; cognitive symptoms appear secondary to mood and stress. F41.1 (generalized anxiety disorder) is less supported as the primary concern, as the patient emphasizes cognitive dysfunction and indecisiveness in the context of low mental energy rather than pervasive anxiety or worry. The persistent 'brain fog,' difficulty concentrating, and impaired decision-making are more consistent with depressive episodes (F32, F33) or adjustment disorder with depressed mood (F43.2). Thus, F06.0 and F41.1 are excluded from current consideration.
